entities.summary:
Diego de Riaño was a Spanish architect of the Renaissance, born in Solórzano, Castile and León, in 1495. He was one of the most outstanding architects of the Plateresque style, known for his innovative designs and use of new materials.








De Riaño's work had a significant impact on the development of architecture in Spain and beyond. His designs influenced a generation of architects, including Juan de Herrera, who went on to become a prominent architect in his own right.









Riaño's legacy extends beyond the world of architecture, as his work reflects the cultural and artistic achievements of the Renaissance. His buildings and designs continue to inspire architects and art historians today.









With a significance score of 7, De Riaño's contributions to the world of architecture are substantial, but not world-changing. His work was regional in scope, with a focus on the development of the Plateresque style in Spain.
